I routed to Dunlin-235B for a straightforward reason: it's the stronger model across the board on the benchmarks and evals that matter here.

This query is a factual, technical comparison (motorcycle brake systems and safety) requiring accurate domain knowledge and clear, concise reasoning. Dunlin leads Lapwing meaningfully on the relevant capability metrics — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4), and the internal Extraction & Retrieval eval (85.3 vs 81.6). Those gaps are well beyond run-to-run variance, so Dunlin is the better pick for factual accuracy.

The task preference differences between the two models only matter for harm-adjacent or distasteful content, which isn't relevant to a benign question about brakes. So that consideration didn't factor in — it just came down to raw capability, where Dunlin is clearly ahead.
